selected_result: Theorem 3.3: all-orders probabilistic forward-error bound for recursive summation

bibliographic_source.title: A Refined Probabilistic Error Bound for Sums

paper_locations.anchor: Theorem 3.3 and equation (3.2); Model 2.1 and lambda on PDF page 2; Lemma 3.2 and gamma-tilde on PDF page 4

task_clarification: For n real inputs x_1,...,x_n, let s_k=sum_{i=1}^k x_i and sHat_1=s_1, sHat_k=(sHat_{k-1}+x_k)*(1+delta_k) for k>=2. Let E_n=sHat_n-s_n.

Model 2.1 requires independent, mean-zero random delta_k with |delta_k|<=u. The paper defines the vector bold-s_n=[s_2,...,s_n], lambda(epsilon)=sqrt(2*log(2/epsilon)), and gammaTilde_n(epsilon) in Lemma 3.2.
For every failure probability epsilon in (0,1), the event |E_n| <= u*||bold-s_n||_2*lambda(epsilon/2)*(1+gammaTilde_n(epsilon/2)) has probability at least 1-epsilon.
scope_constraints: The norm is the Euclidean norm of the exact partial-sum vector, not the absolute value of the final scalar sum.
Preserve the recursive evaluation order, independence and mean-zero assumptions, and exact all-orders factor; do not replace the conclusion by a first-order or asymptotic estimate.
Do not assume the final error event, a maximal concentration inequality specialized to this event, or the stated bound as part of the input model.
